verdict.rationale: Aider's docs say users can request new features or bug fixes in natural language and let aider edit the files in their repo. It can work out which files need editing on its own, and it uses a whole-repository map for context. Community users report it delivering on existing codebases, though one notes subtle errors in its output. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of coordinated multi-file edits for a single request, and independent hands-on corroboration of cross-file feature or bug-fix quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can describe a feature or bug in plain language and have the agent implement or fix it across multiple files

citations.quote: Request new features, test cases or bug fixes using your voice and let aider do the work of editing the files in your local git repo.
You can use aider without adding any files, and it will try to figure out which files need to be edited based on your requests.
Aider takes a `--message` argument, where you can give it a natural language instruction. It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.
Aider uses a **concise map of your whole git repository** that includes the most important classes and functions along with their types and call signatures.
